corridors.name: J14 north - Rosh Pina
notes: The published airway north from Netanya to the Rosh Pina VOR: NAT-MOCEV-GAFAZ-BARZI-ROP. The northern sector is IDFAF ACC 'PLUTO control'.
corridors.src: AIP Israel ENR 3.1 (J14); ENR 2.1 (northern sector, PLUTO control)

corridors.name: The coast road north
notes: Up the coast through LLR01, the IDF/AF offshore training area (7,000-40,000 ft), to the Lebanon border at Rosh HaNikra.
corridors.src: AIP Israel ENR 3.1 (J15 ATLIT); ENR 5.1 LLR01

corridors.name: The Bekaa road
notes: Over Lebanon: the coast, then the Bekaa - Zahle, Baalbek - to the border towns of Ras Baalbek and Al-Fakhah, from where Homs, Masyaf and T-4 are struck. Reported low over the border 2017; stand-off from Lebanese airspace 2018.
corridors.src: Anadolu 2 Nov 2017; Times of Israel / Defense Post 9 Apr 2018 (T-4); Times of Israel 9 Apr 2022; Wikipedia Mole Cricket 19

corridors.name: The sea road - west of Tripoli
notes: Offshore all the way: Sidon, Beirut, Tripoli, then the gate west of Tripoli for the Latakia and Tartus coast. 'Approached Latakia at low altitude from the Mediterranean' (2018).
corridors.src: TASS 18 Sep 2018; The War Zone 2018; Al Jazeera 28 Dec 2021, 2 Jul 2022

corridors.name: The Golan road - Hermon
notes: Rosh Pina, the Hula valley, then over Mount Hermon into the Damascus basin. 1973: low over Jordan, pop up over the Golan, away west of Hermon; 2013: 'entered the Syrian airspace via Mount Hermon'.
corridors.src: Al Jazeera 31 Jan 2013; GlobalSecurity MML (1973); Al Jazeera 24 Nov 2020, 17 Sep 2022

corridors.name: The Amman road - Al-Tanf
notes: The published L200 airway across Jordan - Amman, past Azraq, to the Iraqi corner - and the Al-Tanf deconfliction zone: 'the planes used Jordanian airspace and were aided by American forces stationed at the Tanf garrison'. The route 'enables Israeli forces to avoid Syrian early-warning radar'.
corridors.src: CARC AMDT 19/2022 (L200); Times of Israel 9 Sep 2019; Washington Institute; Al Jazeera 20 Nov 2024

corridors.name: Recovery down the coast
notes: Back through the LLR01 block to the Netanya VOR and home; 'TEL-AVIV control' 121.4 over the water.
corridors.src: AIP Israel ENR 2.1 / 3.1 / 5.1

corridors.name: Recovery via Rosh Pina
notes: Off Hermon back over the Rosh Pina VOR and down J14.
corridors.src: AIP Israel ENR 3.1 (J14)

corridors.name: Recovery down the Amman road
notes: L200 westbound: the Iraqi corner, Azraq, Amman, the Jordan valley at MUVIN.
corridors.src: CARC AMDT 19/2022 (L200)

corridors.name: EAST SID 3 - IREFA
notes: Runway heading, no turns before DER, direct IREFA; 'Aircraft departing Akrotiri going Eastbound are to be flight planned by IREFA'. Flamingo Ops 234.05 outbound.
corridors.src: UK Mil AIP LCRA AD 2.22 and SID EAST 3

corridors.name: WEST SID 1 - ANANE
notes: Runway heading to 580/1880 ft, then direct ANANE - the westbound and the southern-sea departure.
corridors.src: UK Mil AIP LCRA SID WEST 1

corridors.name: The Levant sea road
notes: IREFA to NIKAS, the Damascus FIR entry off Latakia - across the sea south of the Il-20 position of 2018. Russian sea-closure areas off Latakia are declared by NOTAM; their polygons are not published.
corridors.src: UK Mil AIP LCRA; Syria eAIP ENR 3 (R785 NIKAS); safeairspace Cyprus

corridors.name: The Amman run
notes: IREFA to the Israeli coast at MERVA, the Netanya VOR, and the Jordan border at MUVIN - the Akrotiri-to-Iraq run 'via downtown Amman'. Continues on the Amman road to Al-Tanf.
corridors.src: The Aviationist 5 Feb 2019 (Tornado GR4, 'via downtown Amman Jordan'); AIP Israel ENR 3.1 (MERVA, NAT, MUVIN)

corridors.name: STAR ALPHA - the TACAN
notes: From IREFA 'AKR 291 to 15.7 DME', the 13.7 DME arc; hold AKR 189R/11.7d FL100-FL140; talkdown 125.7.
corridors.src: UK Mil AIP LCRA STAR ALPHA / TAC Rwy 28

corridors.name: W74 east - the Northern Watch road
notes: The airway east across south-east Turkey to the Diyarbakır MTMA - the 'ROZ over eastern Turkey' where the Northern Watch package topped off before turning south, the Syrian border 20 miles to the right.
corridors.src: AIP Türkiye ENR 3.1 (W74) / ENR 4.4; A&SF Feb 2000; Ricks/WaPo 25 Oct 2000; GAO OSI-98-4

corridors.name: The Hatay gate - TUNLA
notes: Adana VOR, Hatay VOR, then TUNLA on the FIR boundary south of Hatay - the Syrian coast and the Orontes valley (L601 TUNLA-SALIM-KTN).
corridors.src: AIP Türkiye ENR 4.4 (TUNLA, HTY); Syria eAIP ENR 3 (L601)

corridors.name: The Kilis gate - NISAP
notes: W74 to MILBA then south to NISAP on the border near Kilis; Aleppo is 40 nm beyond (M861 NISAP-ALE).
corridors.src: AIP Türkiye ENR 4.4 (NISAP); Syria eAIP ENR 3 (M861)

corridors.name: The Nusaybin gate - LESRI
notes: From the Diyarbakır MTMA south to LESRI on the border near Nusaybin; Qamishli, Hasakah and the Euphrates beyond (L573 KML-LESRI, L572 to Deir ez-Zor).
corridors.src: AIP Türkiye ENR 4.4 (LESRI); Syria eAIP ENR 3 (L572/L573)

corridors.name: Recovery to Incirlik
notes: Back along W74 into the Adana MTMA (50 nm, FL280 down to 2,000): İncirlik Approach 120.2, TACAN DAN Ch 21X.
corridors.src: AIP Türkiye ENR 2.1 (Adana MTMA); LTAG AD 2

corridors.name: Recovery from the east - the ROZ
notes: Out through LESRI, into the ROZ at Diyarbakır for gas, then W74 westbound - the Northern Watch return.
corridors.src: A&SF Feb 2000; AIP Türkiye ENR 3.1 (W74)

corridors.name: Amman TMA departure
notes: Out of the Amman TMA (5,500-FL155, Class C, 128.9) to ASLON on the L200/A412 corridor that OJP9 leaves open.
corridors.src: CARC ENR 2.1 (Amman TMA); AMDT 19/2022 (ASLON-NADEK excluded from OJP9)

corridors.name: L200 east - Al-Tanf
notes: The Amman-Baghdad airway to the Iraqi corner, then the Al-Tanf zone: 'a 55-kilometer radius from the al-Tanf base'. Muwaffaq Salti is 'significantly closer to At Tanf than Al Dhafra'.
corridors.src: CARC AMDT 19/2022 (L200); VOA / Military Times 2017; TWZ 2019

corridors.name: L513 north - Busra
notes: The Amman-Damascus airway north to BUSRA on the FIR boundary; RDIMA and Damascus beyond (L513).
corridors.src: CARC AMDT 19/2022 (L513); Syria eAIP ENR 3 (L513)

corridors.name: A412 - Zelaf
notes: A412 to ZELAF on the FIR boundary; Palmyra (TUDMU) and the central desert beyond (B544 TAN-TUDMU-ALE).
corridors.src: CARC AMDT 19/2022 (A412); Syria eAIP ENR 3

corridors.name: Recovery to Azraq
notes: L200 westbound into the Amman TMA.
corridors.src: CARC AMDT 19/2022 (L200)

corridors.name: Recovery via Busra
notes: L513 southbound, then east into the Azraq field.
corridors.src: CARC AMDT 19/2022 (L513)

text.brief_title: LEVANT CORRIDORS - HOW YOU GET TO THE FIGHT
brief_intro: The flight plan is threaded through the published structure - the airways and
FIR boundary fixes of the Israeli, Jordanian, Turkish, Cypriot and Syrian AIPs -
and the roads the IAF is reported to fly: over the Bekaa, west of Tripoli, over
Hermon, via Al-Tanf. Israel's northern sector is PLUTO control; Jordan's Amman
TMA is Class C; Incirlik's MTMA is 50 nm; NATO's Akrotiri talks to Flamingo Ops.
brief_sources: Sources: AIP Israel ENR 2.1/3.1/5.1; CARC Jordan ENR 2.1/3.1 and AMDT 19/2022; AIP
Turkiye ENR 2.1/3.1/4.4/5.1; UK Mil AIP LCRA; Syria GACA eAIP ENR 3/4; press
reporting of IAF strikes 2013-2024 (Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, TASS, TWZ, Anadolu);
known_issues: DCS draws no airways or FIR boundaries; the corridors and gates on the F10 map are ours, from the published structure. The AI controllers do not know PLUTO, Flamingo Ops or the Amman TMA exist.
text.sources_line: AIP Israel · CARC Jordan · AIP Türkiye · UK Mil AIP LCRA · Syria GACA eAIP · Al Jazeera / ToI / TASS / TWZ 2013-2024 · GlobalSecurity MML 1973 · Wikipedia
legend: Restricted area: navy, hatched (Israel's LLR training blocks, the Negev ranges; LLP prohibited areas cross-hatched). Control area / CTR: thin dashed blue. Firing area: dashed magenta. Deconfliction zone / line: dashed amber.

Gate ring = the entry/exit point of a road. Fix triangle = a published fix (AIP). ~ = curated: a reported road placed on the named town or summit, or an outline merged/approximated. Coast and borders are schematic.
